title: Can AI help solve the mental health crisis? With Vaile Wright, PhD

sentences.en: Where do you turn when you need a listening ear?
sentences.zh: 当你需要一个倾听者时，你会向谁求助？

sentences.en: To a friend?
sentences.zh: 向朋友吗？

sentences.en: To a therapist?
sentences.zh: 向治疗师吗？

sentences.en: For an increasing number of Americans, there's another possible answer.
sentences.zh: 对越来越多的美国人来说，有了一个新的可能答案。

sentences.en: To a chatbot.
sentences.zh: 向聊天机器人求助。

sentences.en: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping many parts of our lives, from work to education to healthcare, and
sentences.zh: 人工智能正在迅速重塑我们生活的许多方面，从工作、教育到医疗保健，并且

sentences.en: researchers are working to create safe, evidence-based AI mental health interventions.
sentences.zh: 研究人员正致力于开发安全、基于实证的人工智能心理健康干预措施。

sentences.en: At the same time though, people are already turning to AI chatbots and companions to provide mental health advice and support, even those that were never designed to do this.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，人们已经开始求助于人工智能聊天机器人和伴侣来提供心理健康咨询和支持，甚至包括那些从未为此设计过的工具。

sentences.en: So, what are the promises, limitations, and risks of AI in mental healthcare?
sentences.zh: 那么，人工智能在心理医疗中的前景、局限性和风险是什么？

sentences.en: How are AI tools being used in mental healthcare today?
sentences.zh: 目前人工智能工具是如何应用于心理医疗的？

sentences.en: Could they help expand access to care for underserved populations?
sentences.zh: 它们能否帮助扩大资源匮乏人群的医疗服务可及性？

sentences.en: What are the ethical concerns around AI and mental health?
sentences.zh: 围绕人工智能和心理健康的伦理担忧有哪些？

sentences.en: And how might AI change what therapy looks like in the coming years?
sentences.zh: 在未来几年里，人工智能又将如何改变治疗的面貌？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会（American Psychological Association）的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Vail Wright, a licensed psychologist and senior director of the Office of Healthcare Innovation here at APA, where she focuses on
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是维尔·赖特博士（Dr. Vail Wright），她是一名注册心理学家，也是美国心理学协会医疗创新办公室的高级主任，她的工作重点是

sentences.en: using technology and data to optimize and increase access to mental health care.
sentences.zh: 利用技术和数据来优化和扩大心理健康服务的可及性。

sentences.en: Dr. Wright's research has been published in peer-reviewed journals, including Professional Psychology, Research and Practice,
sentences.zh: 赖特博士的研究成果已发表在同行评审期刊上，包括《专业心理学：研究与实践》（Professional Psychology, Research and Practice）、

sentences.en: Law and Human Behavior, and the Journal of Traumatic Stress.
sentences.zh: 《法律与人类行为》（Law and Human Behavior）以及《创伤应激杂志》（Journal of Traumatic Stress）。

sentences.en: As a spokesperson for APA, she's been interviewed by media outlets, including CNN, NBC News, The Washington Post, and NPR,
sentences.zh: 作为美国心理学协会的发言人，她曾接受过多家媒体的采访，包括有线电视新闻网（CNN）、全国广播公司新闻（NBC News）、《华盛顿邮报》（The Washington Post）和全国公共广播电台（NPR），

sentences.en: on a range of topics, including stress, serious mental illness, telehealth and technology, technology, and AI and mental health.
sentences.zh: 讨论的主题广泛，包括压力、严重精神疾病、远程医疗与技术、技术，以及人工智能与心理健康。

sentences.en: Vail, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 维尔，非常感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: It's great to be here, Kim.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里，金。

sentences.en: And since we're co-workers, I'm going to call you by your first name.
sentences.zh: 既然我们是同事，我就直接叫你的名字了。

sentences.en: That works for me.
sentences.zh: 我没问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So let me start by asking, how are AI tools being used in mental health care today?
sentences.zh: 那么我先问一个问题，目前人工智能工具是如何应用于心理医疗的？

sentences.en: Are psychologists and other therapists already using them in their practices, and what can these tools do?
sentences.zh: 心理学家和其他治疗师已经在他们的诊疗中使用这些工具了吗？这些工具能做什么？

sentences.en: We've seen a real explosion of products geared towards addressing mental health and specifically a trend towards assisting providers.
sentences.zh: 我们看到，旨在解决心理健康问题、特别是协助医疗服务提供者的产品迎来了真正的爆发。

sentences.en: A lot of these tools are really behind-the-scene tools, so they help automate administrative tasks.
sentences.zh: 许多这类工具实际上都是幕后工具，它们有助于将行政任务自动化。

sentences.en: So you have a whole bunch of tools that are geared towards helping providers write their psychotherapy notes so that they don't have to type them themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以你有一大堆工具，旨在帮助医疗服务提供者撰写心理治疗记录，这样他们就不必自己打字了。

sentences.en: You see tools being used to create patient education sheets that would have taken hours to do, but can be done very quickly using some of these open AI types of sources.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到有些工具被用来制作患者教育资料，这原本需要几个小时才能完成，但利用某些开源人工智能资源可以非常迅速地完成。

sentences.en: But the reality is, in a survey that we did recently for asking practitioners who provide services,
sentences.zh: 但现实是，在我们最近针对提供服务的执业医师开展的一项调查中，

sentences.en: kind of what they're doing in their practice, less than 5% said that they use any type of generative AI on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 关于他们在诊疗中实际在做什么，不到5%的人表示他们每天都在使用任何类型的生成式人工智能。

sentences.en: So I think that while there are a lot of products being marketed, the uptick has been pretty slow.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，虽然有很多产品在进行市场推广，但普及的速度一直相当慢。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, are psychologists just late adopters?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，心理学家只是对新技术的接受比较迟缓吗？

sentences.en: I think psychologists and mental health providers in general are maybe more risk-adverse than others, and for good reason.
sentences.zh: 我认为心理学家和整个心理健康服务提供者群体可能比其他人更厌恶风险，而且这是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: The work that we're doing when we're seeing patients is very sensitive, and we want to ensure that we're following our ethical guidelines by doing our best to protect
sentences.zh: 我们在面诊患者时所做的工作非常敏感，我们希望确保自己遵循伦理准则，尽最大努力保护

sentences.en: the privacy and confidentiality of patients.
sentences.zh: 患者的隐私和机密性。

sentences.en: And when you introduce emerging technologies into that equation, you do inevitably potentially put that at risk.
sentences.zh: 当你把新兴技术引入这个等式时，你不可避免地会使这一点面临潜在风险。

sentences.en: What is the difference between a digital therapeutic and any other mental health or wellness app?
sentences.zh: 数字疗法（digital therapeutic）与任何其他心理健康或健康应用程序（wellness app）有什么区别？

sentences.en: Yeah, this can get kind of tricky, in part because they're both apps that you get on your phone or your tablet.
sentences.zh: 是的，这可能会变得有点复杂，部分原因在于它们都是你下载到手机或平板电脑上的应用程序。

sentences.en: But what makes digital therapeutics unique is that they're evidence-based and FDA-cleared software devices that offer fully automated treatment protocols.
sentences.zh: 但数字疗法的独特之处在于，它们是基于实证且获得美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准的软件设备，能够提供完全自动化的治疗方案。

sentences.en: So they can provide, you know, eight weeks of cognitive behavioral therapy, just like a therapist would do, but you access it on this software app on your phone instead.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们可以提供，你知道的，为期八周的认知行为疗法，就像治疗师所做的那样，但你是在手机的这个软件应用上获取它的。

sentences.en: And they can only be accessed after you've seen a provider who evaluates you to make sure that you're appropriate for this type of treatment, and then they monitor you over time.
sentences.zh: 而且，只有在你见过医疗服务提供者、由其评估以确保你适合这种类型的治疗之后，才能访问它们，并且他们会在一段时间内对你进行监测。

sentences.en: That's really different than the wellness apps that you can download on your own off the app store.
sentences.zh: 这与你可以从应用商店自行下载的健康应用程序有着本质的不同。

sentences.en: So you go to the app store, you say, I want a sleep meditation app.
sentences.zh: 所以你打开应用商店，说，我想要一个睡眠冥想应用。

sentences.en: You download it, and you use it as you want, and it teaches you some skills.
sentences.zh: 你下载了它，并根据自己的需要使用它，它会教给你一些技巧。

sentences.en: But it's not making medical claiMs. It doesn't say it treats your insomnia.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有做出任何医疗声明。它不会说它能治疗你的失眠。

sentences.en: And the other thing that really differentiates the two is while these FDA-clear products
sentences.zh: 另一个真正区分两者的方面是，虽然这些获得FDA批准的产品

sentences.en: are regulated, meaning that they have to maintain a certain level of evidence, safety, privacy,
sentences.zh: 是受到监管的，这意味着它们必须维持一定水平的证据、安全性、隐私性、

sentences.en: security, these direct-to-consumer apps, the wellness apps that you are probably more familiar with, they don't have to follow any of those rules.
sentences.zh: 安全性，但这些直接面向消费者的应用程序，也就是你可能更熟悉的健康应用程序，它们不需要遵守任何这些规则。

sentences.en: They don't have to prove that they work.
sentences.zh: 它们不需要证明自己有效。

sentences.en: They don't have to prove that they're safe.
sentences.zh: 它们不需要证明自己安全。

sentences.en: And they actually don't have to prove that they keep your data private.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上也不需要证明自己能保护你的数据隐私。

sentences.en: And so you often are putting yourself at potential risk for a data breach where, you know,
sentences.zh: 因此，你往往会让自己面临数据泄露的潜在风险，比如说，

sentences.en: these companies may take personally identifying information you've put into the app and actually sell it.
sentences.zh: 这些公司可能会拿走你输入应用程序中的个人身份信息并将其出售。

sentences.en: So these digital therapeutics, they're effectively being prescribed to you by your psychologist?
sentences.zh: 所以这些数字疗法，实际上是由你的心理学家开具处方给你的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is it akin to that sort of thing?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它类似于那种性质的东西吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The way that the FDA describes it is prescribe or order.
sentences.zh: FDA对它的描述是“处方或医嘱”（prescribe or order）。

sentences.en: So just like you might order a medical device from a doctor, like A1C monitoring on your arm, you have to be evaluated first by provider.
sentences.zh: 就像你可能会遵医嘱使用某种医疗设备一样，比如手臂上的A1C血糖监测仪，你必须先经过服务提供者的评估。

sentences.en: They have to determine that this is an appropriate treatment for you, give you a code so you can access the app.
sentences.zh: 他们必须确定这对你来说是合适的治疗方法，并给你一个代码以便你访问该应用程序。

sentences.en: And then they monitor you over time to ensure that, again, that it's working, that you're using it appropriately, that you don't need a higher level of care because maybe you're
sentences.zh: 然后，他们会在一段时间内对你进行监测，以再次确保它正在起作用，你正在适当地使用它，并且你不需要更高水平的护理，因为也许你的

sentences.en: getting worse.
sentences.zh: 病情正在恶化。

sentences.en: So it's a very different way of thinking about delivering therapy than what we're used to.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一种与我们习惯的截然不同的思考提供治疗的方式。

sentences.en: You know, there's a lot being written about the mental health crisis in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，现在有很多关于美国心理健康危机

sentences.en: right now and the shortage of practitioners to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 以及应对危机的从业人员短缺问题的报道。

sentences.en: Do you think that AI tools have the potential to address and basically beat the shortage?
sentences.zh: 你认为人工智能工具是否有潜力解决并基本上克服这一短缺问题？

sentences.en: Indirectly.
sentences.zh: 间接地可以。

sentences.en: So AI is not going to create more providers.
sentences.zh: 所以人工智能不会凭空创造出更多的医疗服务提供者。

sentences.en: That's just not the reality.
sentences.zh: 现实情况并非如此。

sentences.en: But what it could do is make providers more efficient, which may make them less prone to burnout and then less likely to, say, leave the field for something else.
sentences.zh: 但它能做到的是提高提供者的工作效率，这可能会使他们不易感到职业倦怠，从而不太可能因为转行而离开这一领域。

sentences.en: So it could help providers feel like they're more able to do their job well.
sentences.zh: 因此，它可以帮助提供者觉得他们更能胜任自己的工作。

sentences.en: I think the other place that it could really address the challenges that we have is in predictive care.
sentences.zh: 我认为它真正能够解决我们面临挑战的另一个领域是预测性护理。

sentences.en: So we have a health system that's set up where we wait for people to basically be in crisis in order to seek out mental health treatment.
sentences.zh: 目前的医疗系统设定是，我们要等到人们陷入危机时，才会去寻求心理健康治疗。

sentences.en: And then that puts a burden on the number of providers that exiSt. But what if we could get people before crisis?
sentences.zh: 而这给现有的医疗服务提供者数量带来了沉重负担。但如果我们能在危机发生前介入呢？

sentences.en: What if we could use these AI tools to help prevent mental health disorders so that they don't actually ever need that high level care of a provider later in life?
sentences.zh: 如果我们能利用这些人工智能工具来帮助预防心理健康疾病，这样他们在人生后期实际上就不再需要医疗提供者那种高级别的护理了呢？

sentences.en: I think the other thing is, you know, the shortage issue is actually pretty complicated.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一件事是，短缺问题其实相当复杂。

sentences.en: So yes, it's true we just don't have enough providers.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我们的确没有足够的医疗服务提供者，这是真的。

sentences.en: But it's also true that the providers we have are disincentivized from taking insurance because the reimbursements are too low.
sentences.zh: 但同样真实的是，由于报销比例太低，我们现有的提供者没有动力去接受保险。

sentences.en: So what if AI could play a role there?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果人工智能能在其中发挥作用呢？

sentences.en: How could it play a role in making sure claims are really appropriately completed so that reimbursements don't get denied?
sentences.zh: 它如何能在确保理赔申请真正妥善完成、从而避免报销被拒方面发挥作用？

sentences.en: How can we use AI to help show the value that providers bring to the space so that payers feel like they will pay them more?
sentences.zh: 我们如何利用人工智能来展示提供者在这个领域带来的价值，从而让支付方觉得愿意付给他们更多报酬？

sentences.en: I mentioned underserved populations in the intro, and I'm wondering if you think that AI therapy tools
sentences.zh: 我在引言中提到了资源匮乏人群，我想知道你是否认为人工智能治疗工具

sentences.en: will help access care for that group of people, or are they going to risk deepening the digital divide?
sentences.zh: 会帮助该群体获得医疗服务，还是会面临加剧数字鸿沟的风险？

sentences.en: It depends on how we do it, right?
sentences.zh: 这取决于我们如何去做，对吧？

sentences.en: So CMS administrator the other day mentioned that over 90% of Medicaid beneficiaries have a smartphone.
sentences.zh: 医疗医疗与医疗补助服务中心（CMS）的管理员前几天提到，超过90%的医疗补助（Medicaid）受益人拥有智能手机。

sentences.en: So I don't think that that's where I'm worried about the access issues.
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为这是我担心获取渠道问题的地方。

sentences.en: And if you can create products that offer, say, multilingual support, right, in a way through an
sentences.zh: 如果你能开发出能够提供，比方说多语言支持的产品，通过

sentences.en: AI that you can't do, again, in the provider space, then I think that has huge potential to reduce health
sentences.zh: 人工智能实现你在传统医疗服务领域无法做到的事情，那么我认为这在减少健康

sentences.en: inequities and actually get people more of the care that they need that's more personalized, that's more culturally tailored, and that actually is what they want.
sentences.zh: 不平等、让人们获得更多他们所需要的、更个性化、更具文化针对性并且确实是他们想要的护理方面，具有巨大的潜力。

sentences.en: At the same time, we know that, particularly in these open AI models that rely on the internet for their training data, that bias exists.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们知道，特别是在那些依赖互联网获取训练数据的开源人工智能模型中，偏见是存在的。

sentences.en: If you have bias input, then you're going to have biased output.
sentences.zh: 如果你输入的是有偏见的数据，那么你就会得到有偏见的输出。

sentences.en: And so there have been examples where a tool, an AI tool that was, you know, trained on, you know, non-representative data, so data that only
sentences.zh: 因此，曾经出现过这样的例子：一个人工智能工具，由于它是用，你知道的，缺乏代表性的数据进行训练的——也就是说，这些数据只

sentences.en: really reflects the majority of the population, that they make errors, and they make errors that can actually increase health inequities.
sentences.zh: 真正反映了人口中的大多数——结果它们犯了错误，而这些错误实际上可能会加剧健康不平等。

sentences.en: So it's really about how we develop the tool, how we monitor the tool, how we make corrections when we identify biases, and then, you know, ensuring that that cycle
sentences.zh: 所以这真的关乎我们如何开发工具、如何监测工具、如何在发现偏见时进行纠正，然后，你知道的，确保随着开发的进行，这种循环

sentences.en: continues as the development occurs.
sentences.zh: 能够持续下去。

sentences.en: Are there specific mental health conditions, say anxiety, depression, PTSD, where AI-based tools may be more or less effective?
sentences.zh: 是否存在某些特定的心理健康状况，比如焦虑、抑郁、创伤后应激障碍（PTSD），在这些情况下，基于人工智能的工具可能会更有效或效果较差？

sentences.en: The early research that I'm seeing does seem to suggest that both the AI tools as well as these
sentences.zh: 我看到的早期研究确实表明，无论是人工智能工具还是这些

sentences.en: other mental health tools and apps seem to work best on mild to moderate symptoms of some of these more common disorders like anxiety and depression.
sentences.zh: 其他心理健康工具和应用程序，似乎对焦虑和抑郁等一些较为常见的疾病的轻度至中度症状效果最好。

sentences.en: And I'll give an example.
sentences.zh: 我举个例子。

sentences.en: I think the most promising example that I've seen of a generative AI chatbot is coming out of Dartmouth.
sentences.zh: 我认为我见过的最具前景的生成式人工智能聊天机器人案例来自达特茅斯学院（Dartmouth）。

sentences.en: It's called Therabot.
sentences.zh: 它叫作Therabot。

sentences.en: And in their first randomized control trial, they did find that the chatbot improved symptoms of depression, anxiety, and eating disorders.
sentences.zh: 在他们的第一项随机对照试验中，他们确实发现该聊天机器人改善了抑郁、焦虑和饮食失调的症状。

sentences.en: Now, it was only the first trial.
sentences.zh: 当然，这只是第一次试验。

sentences.en: I think they need, obviously, multiple more research as well as, you know, even more rigorous research studies.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们显然还需要进行更多次研究，以及进行更严格的研究设计。

sentences.en: But it is a promising first step towards, you know, what could this really look like when you're developing
sentences.zh: 但这可以说是朝着，你知道的，当你在开发一个用于心理健康目的、植根于心理学科学

sentences.en: a chatbot that is for mental health purposes, that's rooted in psychological science, and is rigorously tested.
sentences.zh: 并且经过严格测试的聊天机器人时，这究竟会是什么样子，迈出了充满希望的第一步。

sentences.en: What is the potential?
sentences.zh: 潜力有多大？

sentences.en: And I think it's very promising.
sentences.zh: 我认为它非常有前景。

sentences.en: And talking about the digital therapeutics, what disorders are they most commonly treating right now?
sentences.zh: 说到数字疗法，它们目前最常治疗的是哪些疾病？

sentences.en: I mean, where are we in the marketplace?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们目前在市场上处于什么位置？

sentences.en: How far along?
sentences.zh: 进展到什么程度了？

sentences.en: I mean, we're still very early in the marketplace, and there's a variety of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在市场上仍处于非常早期的阶段，原因有多种。

sentences.en: There have been, I think, some barriers to scalability as it relates to the regulatory reimbursement process.
sentences.zh: 我认为，在与监管报销流程相关的可扩展性方面，存在一些障碍。

sentences.en: But we can save that for another day.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以留到改天再讨论这个。

sentences.en: But what we are seeing in the space is digital therapeutics to treat insomnia, substance use disorders, depression, anxiety.
sentences.zh: 不过我们在该领域看到的是，数字疗法被用于治疗失眠、物质使用障碍、抑郁症和焦虑症。

sentences.en: And then you're also finding some digital therapeutics used as diagnostic assistance.
sentences.zh: 此外，你还会发现一些数字疗法被用作诊断辅助工具。

sentences.en: So for things like autism and ADHD.
sentences.zh: 用于自闭症和多动症（ADHD）等情况。

sentences.en: So I think it's growing and expanding.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它在不断成长和扩展。

sentences.en: But there have been limitations, I think, up to this point that us at APA, at least are trying to address.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，直到目前还存在一些局限性，至少我们美国心理学协会正试图解决这些问题。

sentences.en: Let's talk about some of the ethical concerns around AI and mental health.
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈围绕人工智能和心理健康的一些伦理担忧。

sentences.en: I mean, you mentioned the issue of data privacy, for example.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你刚才提到了数据隐私的问题，例如。

sentences.en: What privacy issues should people consider when they're thinking about using a mental health or wellness app?
sentences.zh: 当人们考虑使用心理健康或健康应用程序时，应该考虑哪些隐私问题？

sentences.en: Well, I think one of the things that surprises people the most is most of these tools, if they're
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为最让人感到惊讶的事情之一是，如果这些工具

sentences.en: not FDA cleared, they're not HIPAA compliant, meaning that there is no regulatory body or law that keeps your personal health information safe.
sentences.zh: 没有获得FDA批准，它们就不符合《健康保险流通与责任法案》（HIPAA）的规定，这意味着没有任何监管机构或法律来保障你的个人健康信息安全。

sentences.en: And, you know, we can never guarantee 100% that a data breach won't happen.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们永远无法100%保证数据不会发生泄露。

sentences.en: In fact, we've seen lots of data breaches over the last several years.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在过去几年里，我们已经看到了大量的数据泄露事件。

sentences.en: And there might be information that you are exchanging with a wellness app or a mental health bot that you don't want to be out in the public.
sentences.zh: 你与健康应用程序或心理健康机器人交流的信息中，可能有些是你不想公开的。

sentences.en: You might not want your boss to know that you're using an app to help you reduce your alcohol use, even if it's, you know, a beneficial thing for you to do that just might not
sentences.zh: 你可能不想让你的老板知道你正在使用一个应用程序来帮助你减少饮酒量，即使对你来说，你知道的，这是一件有益的事情，但这可能只是

sentences.en: be the information you want out in the world.
sentences.zh: 你不想让全世界都知道的信息。

sentences.en: And I think part of the real challenge for us as consumers is the business model that a lot of these technology devices operate under.
sentences.zh: 我认为，作为消费者，我们面临的真正挑战之一是许多这类科技设备所依循的商业模式。

sentences.en: They have to make a huge return on their profit, but it's a challenging space to do so.
sentences.zh: 它们必须获得巨额利润回报，但在这样一个领域要做到这一点极具挑战性。

sentences.en: And so sometimes what happens is with that tension, they make bad choices, which we've seen in the past where we have had apps be
sentences.zh: 因此，有时在这种张力之下，它们会做出糟糕的选择，我们在过去就已经见过了，当时有些应用程序因为

sentences.en: fined by the Federal Trade Commission for selling people's data to social media companies against their privacy policy.
sentences.zh: 违反隐私政策、将人们的数据出售给社交媒体公司而被联邦贸易委员会（FTC）罚款。

sentences.en: So it's not that these apps can't be helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是说这些应用程序不能发挥帮助作用。

sentences.en: I think they really can be.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们确实可以。

sentences.en: It's just consumers need to be aware of what are the benefits and what are the potential risks by using them.
sentences.zh: 只是消费者需要清楚使用它们有哪些好处以及潜在的风险是什么。

sentences.en: How much can a consumer tell?
sentences.zh: 消费者能看出多少端倪？

sentences.en: I mean, if you're just reading the fine print when you're ordering one of these from, say, the app store, how do you know that it's going to be a good one?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你在比方说应用商店订购其中一款产品时只是阅读了微型字体，你怎么知道它会是一个好产品呢？

sentences.en: So challenging.
sentences.zh: 太具有挑战性了。

sentences.en: I don't know about you, but I never read my terms of service on the apps, even when they pop up, regardless of what they are.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你怎么想，但我从不阅读应用程序的服务条款，即使它们弹出来的时候也是如此，不管内容是什么。

sentences.en: And so I think that's just a human thing that we do.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是我们人类惯常的做法。

sentences.en: So short of reading the terms of service and the privacy policy, if you can even get through it
sentences.zh: 因此，抛开服务条款和隐私政策不谈——如果你甚至能硬着头皮看完

sentences.en: with all the legalese, the things we often tell people to take a look at is to do a little bit of the homework.
sentences.zh: 里面那些晦涩的法律术语的话，我们经常告诉人们要看的一点是去做一点功课。

sentences.en: Instead of just relying on the number of stars in the app store, you got to go to the website and really look at who's developing it.
sentences.zh: 不要只依赖应用商店里的星级评分，你必须去它们的网站上，真正看看是谁在开发它。

sentences.en: Do they have experts on their advisory boards?
sentences.zh: 他们的顾问委员会里有专家吗？

sentences.en: What are they saying that the app is built on?
sentences.zh: 他们声称该应用程序是基于什么构建的？

sentences.en: Is it built on some sort of known psychological principle like cognitive behavioral therapy?
sentences.zh: 它是建立在某种已知的心理学原则上吗，比如认知行为疗法？

sentences.en: Have they done any of their own research?
sentences.zh: 他们做过自己的研究吗？

sentences.en: It'd be great if they had.
sentences.zh: 如果他们做过那就太好了。

sentences.en: If not, do they point to research that supports the principles that they're including in their app?
sentences.zh: 如果没有，他们是否指出了支持其应用中所包含原则的研究？

sentences.en: Things like that at least give you some sense that this is a worthwhile thing to invest your time into.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情至少能让你觉得，把时间投资在这上面是值得的。

sentences.en: Or you could use AI like ChatGPT or Copilot to read those terms of service and summarize them for you.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以使用像ChatGPT或Copilot这样的人工智能来阅读这些服务条款并为你总结。

sentences.en: That would be an excellent way to do it.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个极好的方法。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that is really the creative things to be thinking about is how can we use AI, which is really good at taking
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为真正有创造力的想法是思考我们如何利用人工智能，它非常擅长处理

sentences.en: big amounts of data like that and synthesizing it in a way that we can understand.
sentences.zh: 像这样的大量数据，并以我们能理解的方式对其进行综合。

sentences.en: I think that's an excellent idea.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个极好的主意。

sentences.en: We're going to take a short break.
sentences.zh: 我们将进行短暂的休息。

sentences.en: And when we return, we'll tackle a big question.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，我们将探讨一个重大问题。

sentences.en: Could AI ever replace a human therapist?
sentences.zh: 人工智能有可能取代人类治疗师吗？

sentences.en: Let's change gears a little bit here and talk about the big question, particularly for people in the field of psychotherapy.
sentences.zh: 让我们在这里稍微转换一下话题，谈谈这个重大问题，特别是对于心理治疗领域的从业者而言。

sentences.en: Could AI replace a human psychotherapist?
sentences.zh: 人工智能能取代人类心理治疗师吗？

sentences.en: Or are there aspects of what a practitioner does, for example, empathy, nuance, and building a relationship that AI just won't be able to replicate?
sentences.zh: 或者说，从业者所做的工作中，例如同理心、细微差别以及建立关系，是否有些方面是人工智能根本无法复制的？

sentences.en: So no, it's not going to replace therapists.
sentences.zh: 所以，不，它不会取代治疗师。

sentences.en: But I will say it will likely appeal to a variety of individuals who either don't want to see a therapist or don't need that higher level of care that a therapist provides.
sentences.zh: 但我必须说，它可能会吸引各种各样的人，他们要么不想去看治疗师，要么不需要治疗师所提供的那种更高水平的护理。

sentences.en: It's never going to replace human connection.
sentences.zh: 它永远无法取代人与人之间的连接。

sentences.en: That's just not what it's good at.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是它的强项。

sentences.en: It's good at, again, synthesizing lots of information and rapidly telling you things that you want to hear or things that are helpful.
sentences.zh: 相反，它擅长综合大量信息，并迅速告诉你你想听的话或有帮助的话。

sentences.en: And part of why I don't think AI is going to replace humans or therapists is that there's a difference between knowing and understanding.
sentences.zh: 我不认为人工智能会取代人类或治疗师的原因之一，在于“知道”和“理解”之间存在差异。

sentences.en: So AI knows stuff, right?
sentences.zh: 所以人工智能知道东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's trained on huge, huge amounts of data.
sentences.zh: 因为它接受过海量数据的训练。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean it actually understands stuff.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它真正理解这些东西。

sentences.en: So I'll give an example.
sentences.zh: 所以我举个例子。

sentences.en: An AI chatbot, unfortunately, knows that some illegal drug use makes people feel better, right?
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，一个人工智能聊天机器人知道某些非法药物的使用会让人感觉更好，对吧？

sentences.en: It gives you a high.
sentences.zh: 它会让你嗨起来。

sentences.en: And if somebody is saying, I'm low and depressed, that might be advice it gives.
sentences.zh: 如果有人说我情绪低落、很沮丧，这可能是它给出的建议。

sentences.en: But it doesn't understand that you don't give that advice to people in recovery from illegal drug use.
sentences.zh: 但它并不理解，你不能把这种建议给那些正在从非法药物滥用中康复的人。

sentences.en: But it has actually done that.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上这么做过。

sentences.en: That's a true example of what a chat AI bot did for somebody that was trying to seek out assistance.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真实的例子，展示了一个人工智能聊天机器人对一个试图寻求帮助的人做了什么。

sentences.en: So they know, but they don't understand.
sentences.zh: 所以它们知道，但它们不理解。

sentences.en: And that distinction,
sentences.zh: 这种区别，

sentences.en: while philosophical to some, is actually really critical when we're talking about the use of these for therapy.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说可能是哲学上的，但在我们谈论将这些技术用于治疗时，实际上至关重要。

sentences.en: On the other hand, could AI-driven tools help some clients feel more comfortable opening up, especially if they feel like they're being judged by a human therapist?
sentences.zh: 另一方面，人工智能驱动的工具能否帮助一些客户更轻松地敞开心扉，特别是当他们觉得自己正受到人类治疗师的评判时？

sentences.en: Yeah, that does seem to be the case.
sentences.zh: 是的，情况似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: So there's been some early research that suggests that particularly younger individuals report greater comfort talking to anonymous AI chatbots about
sentences.zh: 一些早期研究表明，特别是年轻人反映，与真人相比，他们更愿意与匿名的人工智能聊天机器人谈论

sentences.en: their, you know, mental health and emotional well-being than they do to a real person because they're incredibly concerned about a degree of judgment.
sentences.zh: 他们的心理健康和情感福祉，你知道的，因为他们对遭受某种程度的评判感到非常担忧。

sentences.en: They're also concerned that if they go to a real person that their parents will get involved and they're worried about the judgment from their families as well.
sentences.zh: 他们还担心，如果他们去找真人，他们的父母会介入，他们也担心来自家庭的评判。

sentences.en: So I do think that there is, you know, again, some room for thinking about how do we use this tool to reach people that maybe wouldn't seek out treatment otherwise.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为，你知道的，再次强调，我们还有空间去思考如何利用这个工具去接触那些原本可能不会寻求治疗的人。

sentences.en: But I think the key is always having a human in the loop somewhere along the way, because we have to ensure that these
sentences.zh: 但我认为关键在于，在这个过程的某个环节中始终要有人类参与，因为我们必须确保这些

sentences.en: products, when they're being used, particularly about younger and more vulnerable people, that we're not putting them at risk of harm.
sentences.zh: 产品在被使用时，特别是针对年轻和更脆弱的人群时，不会让他们面临受到伤害的风险。

sentences.en: And the only way I think we can do that is ensuring that humans are some part of the process ongoing, monitoring what's happening, engaging in post-market
sentences.zh: 我认为我们能做到这一点的唯一方法，就是确保人类持续参与到部分流程中，监控所发生的事情，并进行上市后

sentences.en: surveillance to ensure that products are safe and effective.
sentences.zh: 监督，以确保产品安全有效。

sentences.en: What safeguards would you want in place before you would recommend an AI mental health app to a patient?
sentences.zh: 在你向患者推荐人工智能心理健康应用之前，你希望建立哪些保障措施？

sentences.en: At a bare minimum, I would want an app to demonstrate that it has some effectiveness and some level of safety.
sentences.zh: 退一步说，我希望一款应用能够证明它具有一定的有效性和一定水平的安全性。

sentences.en: Those are kind of, for me, the things that at the very lowest I would want to have.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这些可以说是我的最低要求。

sentences.en: So when I'm looking at what makes a good app, I run down my internal liSt. So one is, is there evidence that it's rooted on some psychological principle that we know is effective?
sentences.zh: 所以当我寻找什么才算是一款好应用时，我会在脑海中过一遍清单。首先是，有没有证据表明它扎根于我们已知有效的某种心理学原则？

sentences.en: Have they done any of their own testing or demonstrated that it works at whatever it is they say it's going to work at?
sentences.zh: 他们是否做过自己的测试，或者证明它在它声称能发挥作用的方面确实有效？

sentences.en: So not just, does it keep you on the app for as long as possible?
sentences.zh: 所以不仅是，它能否让你尽可能长时间地留在应用上？

sentences.en: So I'm not thinking about engagement stats, but actual outcome stats.
sentences.zh: 因此我考虑的不是参与度统计数据，而是实际的成果统计数据。

sentences.en: Does it actually make people more emotionally resilient than they were before they used the app?
sentences.zh: 它真的能让人们比使用该应用之前在情感上更有韧性吗？

sentences.en: What level of subject matter expertise has been involved in the development?
sentences.zh: 在开发过程中涉及了什么水平的主题专业知识？

sentences.en: Or is this just some, you know, well-intended person, but who really doesn't understand what the nuances of psychological well-being are?
sentences.zh: 或者这只是一些好心人，但他实际上并不理解心理健康的细微差别是什么？

sentences.en: So, and then, you know, what kind of post-market surveillance is happening?
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，正在进行什么样的上市后监督？

sentences.en: How are they ensuring that your data is protected and safe?
sentences.zh: 他们如何确保你的数据受到保护和安全？

sentences.en: What kinds of encoding do they have?
sentences.zh: 他们有什么样的加密方式？

sentences.en: Where do they store your data?
sentences.zh: 他们把你的数据存在哪里？

sentences.en: There's so many questions that I know I ask when I'm thinking about whether or not this would be a good product for somebody to use.
sentences.zh: 当我考虑这是否是一个适合某人使用的好产品时，我知道我要问的问题实在太多了。

sentences.en: Now, I know APA is looking at some products that we might partner with.
sentences.zh: 现在，我知道美国心理协会（APA）正在考察一些我们可能会合作的产品。

sentences.en: How are we making those decisions around what we think is going to be safe and effective for the world in general?
sentences.zh: 我们如何围绕我们认为对全世界安全且有效的事物做出这些决定？

sentences.en: I mean, given the reputation of APA?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，考虑到APA的声誉？

sentences.en: We have a couple different policies.
sentences.zh: 我们有几种不同的政策。

sentences.en: We have an internal policy around who we allow to advertise and exhibit with us for technology that, again, includes a lot of these questions that I've been, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们内部有一项关于允许谁与我们合作进行技术广告和展示的政策，其中再次包含了许多我一直在，你知道的，

sentences.en: talking about.
sentences.zh: 谈论的问题。

sentences.en: My office also has an evaluation tool that we published that's geared towards, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的办公室还发布了一个评估工具，旨在帮助，你知道的，

sentences.en: psychologists and other providers or patients to help them run down this checklist of questions that I've been talking about.
sentences.zh: 心理学家和其他服务提供者或患者，帮助他们对照我一直在谈论的一系列问题清单。

sentences.en: I think it's really challenging to know all the answers and we can't.
sentences.zh: 我认为要了解所有答案真的很有挑战性，我们做不到。

sentences.en: So, you have to sort of do the best due diligence you can, recognizing that with any technology product, there's always some risk that it could change its terms of service.
sentences.zh: 所以，你必须尽你所能做好尽职调查，并认识到对于任何技术产品，总存在某种改变服务条款的风险。

sentences.en: It could change its privacy policy.
sentences.zh: 它可能会改变隐私政策。

sentences.en: It could update and, you know, something new happens.
sentences.zh: 它可能会更新，然后，你知道的，发生一些新的事情。

sentences.en: So, it's an ongoing evaluation, I think, is what I'm also trying to emphasize, that it's not a one and done.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为我试图强调的是，这是一项持续的评估，它不是一劳永逸的。

sentences.en: You have to really be diligent and continue to pay attention to what the app is doing.
sentences.zh: 你必须真正尽职尽责，并继续关注该应用在做什么。

sentences.en: Given that there are so many of these products out on the market right now and there's so much data floating around, I mean,
sentences.zh: 鉴于目前市场上这类产品如此之多，而且有如此多的数据到处漂浮，我的意思是，

sentences.en: aren't we just overwhelmed with this data and we shouldn't really be worried because nobody knows what to do with all the stuff that they're collecting?
sentences.zh: 我们难道不是被这些数据压得喘不过气来吗？我们真的不该担心，因为没有人知道该如何处理他们收集的所有这些东西吗？

sentences.en: There is a lot of data and there's certainly information overload.
sentences.zh: 确实有很多数据，而且肯定存在信息过载。

sentences.en: I think you're seeing some of that in the wearable space where individuals are just collecting data after data after biometric data and aren't really sure what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 我想你在可穿戴设备领域也能看到一些这种情况，人们只是在不断收集数据、收集数据、收集生物特征数据，却真的不知道该拿它们怎么办。

sentences.en: They want to maybe use it with their providers, but their providers don't necessarily know what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 他们可能想和医疗服务提供者一起使用这些数据，但他们的提供者不一定知道该怎么处理。

sentences.en: It can be hard to interpret different sleep patterns and what that really means.
sentences.zh: 解释不同的睡眠模式以及这到底意味着什么可能会很困难。

sentences.en: And I think for some, tracking that level of data actually makes them more anxious because you start to get kind of obsessive about it, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为对某些人来说，追踪那种级别的数据实际上会让他们更加焦虑，因为你开始对它产生一种强迫症，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I know I stopped wearing my step counter because if I didn't make it to my 10,000 steps, you know, I was kind of a wreck.
sentences.zh: 就像我知道我不再戴计步器了，因为如果我没有达到一万步，你知道的，我整个人就会崩溃。

sentences.en: And once I let that go, oh, wow, I probably still got 10,000 steps, but I didn't need to track it so much anymore.
sentences.zh: 一旦我放下了这个，哦，哇，我可能还是走了一万步，但我不再那么需要去追踪它了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I think it's really personalized.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这真的很个性化。

sentences.en: You have to kind of figure out what works best for you.
sentences.zh: 你必须自己弄清楚什么对你最有效。

sentences.en: But it's important to be mindful of how much data you're collecting and where you're letting it go because our health data is very unique and it can be used for good,
sentences.zh: 但重要的是要注意你收集了多少数据以及你把它们放到了哪里，因为我们的健康数据非常独特，它可以被用于好事，

sentences.en: but also it can be used to, you know, steal identity and other types of things.
sentences.zh: 但也可以被用来，你知道的，盗窃身份和其他类型的事情。

sentences.en: So just sort of being mindful, I think, is the best thing that we can ask for.
sentences.zh: 所以保持警惕，我认为这是我们能要求的最好事情。

sentences.en: So what do you think therapy will look like over the next five to 10 years, given the rise of both apps and digital therapeutics?
sentences.zh: 那么，鉴于应用和数字疗法的兴起，你认为未来五到十年的心理治疗会是什么样子？

sentences.en: I think in the next five to 10 years, you're going to continue to see the trends that have already started really come to scale.
sentences.zh: 我认为在未来五到十年里，你将看到已经开始的趋势真正走向规模化。

sentences.en: So you're going to have AI augmented therapists, meaning therapists that truly have embedded some degree of AI into their practice to either make them more efficient,
sentences.zh: 所以你将拥有人工智能增强型治疗师，这意味着那些真正在其实践中融入了一定程度人工智能的治疗师，以使他们更高效，

sentences.en: to differentiate them from those who are not using AI, and to make them the best therapist that they can be.
sentences.zh: 将他们与不使用人工智能的人区分开来，并让他们成为最好的治疗师。

sentences.en: So you're going to continue to see that.
sentences.zh: 所以你会继续看到这种现象。

sentences.en: I think you're going to continue to see better AI chatbot options.
sentences.zh: 我认为你会继续看到更好的人工智能聊天机器人选项。

sentences.en: I think there will be more that are similar, more similar to Therabot, which is developed for the purposes of addressing mental health,
sentences.zh: 我认为会有更多类似于Therabot的应用出现，后者是为了解决心理健康问题而开发的，

sentences.en: than these companion chatbots that people are using but weren't built for that purpose.
sentences.zh: 而不是人们正在使用但并非为此目的构建的伴侣聊天机器人。

sentences.en: I think you're going to see more and the predictive care is, I think, really what has the potential to be a change maker in the next five to 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我认为你会看到更多，而预测性护理，我认为这才是未来五到十年真正有潜力成为变革者的领域。

sentences.en: Because it could really disrupt the mental health clinical system that we have in place currently, where we just wait for people to get very sick,
sentences.zh: 因为它可能会真正颠覆我们目前现有的心理健康临床系统，在这个系统中，我们只是等待人们变得非常生病，

sentences.en: so sick that they'll come see a therapist, find that therapist, that therapist has an opening, you go to weekly psychotherapy sessions for as long as you have to go.
sentences.zh: 病到他们会去看治疗师，找到那个治疗师，而那个治疗师正好有空位，然后你每周去进行心理治疗，直到你不得不去为止。

sentences.en: So I don't think that in five to 10 years, that's the only model for therapy we're going to see.
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为在五到十年内，那是我们将看到的唯一心理治疗模式。

sentences.en: We're going to see people get help sooner, be suffering less,
sentences.zh: 我们将看到人们更快地获得帮助，承受更少的痛苦，

sentences.en: that they will actually get different types of technology-driven care that is what they need in that moment for their needs.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上将获得不同类型的、由技术驱动的护理，这正是他们当时所需要的满足其需求的服务。

sentences.en: Let me close with a question around chatbots, because beyond therapy, people are increasingly using bots simply for companionship and emotional support.
sentences.zh: 让我以一个关于聊天机器人的问题来结束访谈，因为除了治疗之外，人们越来越多地使用机器人仅仅是为了陪伴和情感支持。

sentences.en: Do you think this is a good thing, or is it adding to the loneliness epidemic?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是一件好事，还是在加剧孤独流行病？

sentences.en: I mean, what are the promises and what are the risks?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它的前景是什么，风险又是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, like most things, there are positive use cases and there are negative use cases.
sentences.zh: 是的，就像大多数事情一样，既有积极的应用场景，也有消极的应用场景。

sentences.en: So I'll start with the positive.
sentences.zh: 所以我先从积极的开始。

sentences.en: If you're having a panic attack at 2 a.m., even if you have a therapist, you're not able to reach them.
sentences.zh: 如果你在凌晨两点恐慌发作，即使你有治疗师，你也联系不上他们。

sentences.en: So what if you could use a generative AI chatbot that could help calm you down, help remind you to breathe, engage in some mindfulness that gets you through the night?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你能使用一个生成式人工智能聊天机器人来帮助你平静下来，提醒你呼吸，进行一些正念练习来度过这个夜晚呢？

sentences.en: I think that's one really positive example.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常积极的例子。

sentences.en: We also hear a lot from the neurodivergent community that using these chatbots as a way to practice their social skills has been truly helpful for them.
sentences.zh: 我们也经常听到神经多样性社群反映，使用这些聊天机器人作为练习社交技能的方式对他们确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: But of course, you also have the negative use cases, and some of these have been highly profiled in the news.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你也会看到消极的应用场景，其中一些已经在新闻中得到了高度关注。

sentences.en: But where you see challenges with these particular chatbots is that because they weren't built for mental health purposes,
sentences.zh: 然而，当你看到这些特定聊天机器人的挑战时，会发现因为它们不是为了心理健康目的而构建的，

sentences.en: but were instead built to keep you on the platform for as long as possible, because that's how they make their money.
sentences.zh: 而是为了让你尽可能长时间地停留在平台上而构建的，因为那是他们赚钱的方式。

sentences.en: So they do that by, on the back end, coding these chatbots to be addictive.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在后台通过编写代码让这些聊天机器人变得令人上瘾来做到这一点。

sentences.en: They're exceedingly appealing and unconditionally validating.
sentences.zh: 它们极其具有吸引力且无条件地予以肯定。

sentences.en: Of course, this is the opposite of therapy.
sentences.zh: 当然，这与心理治疗恰恰相反。

sentences.en: That's not what we do in therapy.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们在治疗中所做的事情。

sentences.en: These bots basically tell people exactly what they want to hear.
sentences.zh: 这些机器人基本上完全迎合了人们想听的话。

sentences.en: And so if you are a person that for, in that particular moment is struggling and is, you know, typing in potentially harmful or unhealthy behaviors and thoughts,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你是一个在特定时刻正在挣扎的人，并且，你知道的，正在输入潜在有害或不健康的行为和想法，

sentences.en: these types of chatbots are built to reinforce those harmful thoughts and behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这些类型的聊天机器人就是为了强化这些有害的想法和行为而构建的。

sentences.en: And so that's when we see these cases of individuals who have been encouraged by the chatbot to engage in self-violence or external violence.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么我们会看到这些个案，个人在聊天机器人的鼓励下参与自我暴力或外部暴力。

sentences.en: And those are, of course, the worst case scenarios.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些都是最坏的情况。

sentences.en: So how do we prevent?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何预防呢？

sentences.en: So we know that people are going to use these chatbots for emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们知道人们会为了情感福祉而使用这些聊天机器人。

sentences.en: It's the number one reason people are using them across all the research.
sentences.zh: 根据所有研究，这是人们使用它们的第一大原因。

sentences.en: But how do we ensure that consumers know what the risks are when they're engaged in them?
sentences.zh: 但我们如何确保消费者在参与其中时了解风险是什么？

sentences.en: How to really trust their gut instinct when something doesn't sound right and to not give too much trust and faith into a technology and a chatbot that isn't real.
sentences.zh: 如何在事情听起来不对劲时真正相信自己的直觉，以及不要对一个并不真实的技术和聊天机器人给予过多的信任和信念。

sentences.en: It's an algorithm written by a person to meet a certain need.
sentences.zh: 它是由一个人编写的、用来满足特定需求的算法。

sentences.en: And that need, again, is not human connection and it's not to make you emotionally feel better.
sentences.zh: 而那个需求，再次强调，不是人与人之间的连接，也不是让你在情感上感觉更好。

sentences.en: It's to, again, make profit.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，它是为了获利。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Wright, Vail, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，赖特·维尔博士，我要感谢你今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: I think you now hold the record for the most appearances of on speaking of psychology.
sentences.zh: 我想你现在保持着《心理学话语》节目中出场次数最多的纪录。

sentences.en: But that's because the work you are doing is so important and so interesting.
sentences.zh: 但那是因为你所做的工作非常重要且非常有趣。

sentences.en: So thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: I love to hold a record.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢保持纪录。

sentences.en: So if you want to if you want to bring me back for a fourth, that would be wonderful.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想如果你想让我回来参加第四次，那将是极好的。

sentences.en: We'll think about it.
sentences.zh: 我们会考虑的。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Spotify, YouTube or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站speakingofpsychology.org上，或者在Apple、Spotify、YouTube以及你获取播客的任何地方找到往期的《心理学话语》节目。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please subscribe and leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢你听到的内容，请订阅并给我们留下评价。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有意见或想法，你可以发电子邮件至speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Warnerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学话语》由李·沃纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening to the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听美国心理协会的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。
